_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Seychelles covering uninhabited period, French settlement, British colony, spice trade, independence 1976, René coup and socialism, democratic transition, ocean conservation, and tourism economy.

ethnic_groups.name: Seychellois Creole
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed African, European (French/British), Indian, Chinese, and Malagasy descent; Creole (Kreol Seselwa) language; Catholic; no indigenous population

ethnic_groups.name: French descent
ethnic_groups.notes: Grand Blancs and Petits Blancs; original settler families; historically plantation-owning elite

ethnic_groups.name: Indian descent
ethnic_groups.notes: Gujarati, Tamil communities; arrived 19th–20th century; commerce and trade

country_profile.notes_unique:
Smallest African nation by population; highest GDP per capita in Africa; 115 islands; Ald
abra Atoll UNESCO site; coco de mer palm

current_leader.name: Wavel Ramkalawan
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: LDS party; Anglican priest; first opposition president; ended 43 years of SPPF/PL rule

former_presidents.name: James Mancham
former_presidents.notes: First president; SDP; pro-Western; overthrown by René's coup while at Commonwealth summit

former_presidents.name: France-Albert René
former_presidents.notes: SPPF; socialist one-party state 1977–1993; survived multiple coup attempts; transitioned to multiparty 1993; retired voluntarily

former_presidents.name: James Michel
former_presidents.notes: SPPF/PL; René's ally; Blue Economy advocate; resigned

former_presidents.name: Danny Faure
former_presidents.notes: PL; completed Michel's term; lost to Ramkalawan 2020

910.name: Geological Formation and Pre-Human History
910.description: Ancient granitic islands of Gondwana origin; no indigenous human population; Austronesian and Arab sailors may have visited.

sub_clusters.name: Gondwana Granitic Islands
sub_clusters.description: Seychelles granitic islands as ancient Gondwana continental fragments; oldest mid-ocean islands on Earth.

sub_clusters.name: Uninhabited Archipelago
sub_clusters.description: No evidence of permanent pre-European settlement; possible visits by Austronesian and Arab-Persian sailors.

920.name: Early Sightings and Arab Knowledge
920.description: Arab and Maldivian traders aware of the islands; Portuguese sightings but no settlement.

sub_clusters.name: Arab and Maldivian Awareness
sub_clusters.description: Arab navigators and Maldivian fishermen likely aware of Seychelles; references to 'zarin' (high islands) in Arab texts.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Sightings
sub_clusters.description: Vasco da Gama expedition sights islands 1502; mapped as Amirantes; no colonisation attempt.

930.name: French Settlement and Colonisation
930.description: French East India Company claims islands; named after Moreau de Séchelles; spice plantations established; strategic Indian Ocean position.

sub_clusters.name: Lazare Picault Expedition
sub_clusters.description: Lazare Picault explores islands 1742; France formally claims and names them Séchelles 1756.

sub_clusters.name: First Permanent Settlement
sub_clusters.description: First French settlers with enslaved workers arrive 1770; spice gardens established; small plantation colony.

sub_clusters.name: Capitulations to Britain
sub_clusters.description: Seychelles governor Quéau de Quincy capitulates to British navy seven times while maintaining French administration; pragmatic neutrality.

940.name: British Colonial Period
940.description: Treaty of Paris cedes Seychelles to Britain; crown colony; coconut/copra economy; Creole society; path to independence.

sub_clusters.name: Treaty of Paris and British Rule
sub_clusters.description: Treaty of Paris 1814 cedes Seychelles to Britain; administered from Mauritius; abolition of slavery 1835.

sub_clusters.name: Crown Colony Status
sub_clusters.description: Seychelles becomes separate crown colony 1903; copra and vanilla economy; political exile destination.

sub_clusters.name: Spice and Plantation Economy
sub_clusters.description: Coconut, vanilla, cinnamon, and copra exports; plantation-based economy; Creole workforce.

sub_clusters.name: Seychellois Creole Society
sub_clusters.description: Unique Creole culture blending French, African, Indian, and Chinese heritage; Seselwa Creole language develops.

950.name: Independence and René Era
950.description: Self-governance; independence 1976 under Mancham; René coup 1977; one-party socialist state; Cold War positioning.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Seychelles
sub_clusters.description: Independence 29 June 1976; James Mancham first president; coalition government.

sub_clusters.name: France-Albert René Coup
sub_clusters.description: France-Albert René overthrows Mancham in bloodless coup 5 June 1977; establishes one-party socialist state.

sub_clusters.name: One-Party Socialist Period
sub_clusters.description: SPPF one-party rule; socialist policies; repelled South African-backed mercenary coup attempt 1981; Cold War non-alignment.

960.name: Democratic Transition and Modern Seychelles
960.description: Multiparty democracy restored; tourism-based economy; marine conservation leadership; blue economy.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Transition
sub_clusters.description: Multiparty constitution adopted 1993; René wins democratic elections; peaceful transition.

sub_clusters.name: Tourism-Driven Economy
sub_clusters.description: Luxury tourism becomes economic mainstay; high per-capita GDP for Africa; vulnerability to global shocks.

sub_clusters.name: Marine Conservation Leadership
sub_clusters.description: Seychelles pioneers debt-for-nature swaps; 30% marine protection; blue economy strategy; coral reef conservation.

sub_clusters.name: Political Alternation and Governance
sub_clusters.description: Opposition LDS coalition wins 2016 parliamentary majority; Ramkalawan wins presidency 2020; peaceful transfers of power.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
